title: Fix it: build the tag list for a shop's filter menu
basics: `flatten` turns an Array of Arrays into one Array: `flatten([[1], [2, 3]])` is `[1, 2, 3]`. Selecting a field from an Array of objects, `payload.tags`, collects that field from every element.
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

Products arrive as `{ sku, tags }`. The filter menu needs every tag used by any product, **once each**, in lower case, sorted alphabetically.

Merchandisers typed the tags, so the same tag can appear as `Sale` and `sale`. Some products have no `tags` field at all.

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
starter:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload flatMap $.tags map lower($)) distinctBy $ orderBy $
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
uses flatMap, which turns a product with no tags into a null tag, and a null cannot be sorted with the Strings
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(flatten(payload.tags default []) map lower($)) distinctBy $ orderBy $

mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload flatMap $.tags map lower($)) distinctBy $ orderBy $

explanation.approach: Selecting `.tags` across the products gives an Array of Arrays and simply skips products with no tags. `flatten` makes it one list. Normalising the case has to happen before deduplication, because `distinctBy` compares exactly.

snippets.label: Selecting across products
snippets.note: The product with no tags contributes nothing.

snippets.label: flatMap on a missing field
snippets.note: The product with no tags contributes a null element instead of nothing, and `lower` then passes it on as null.
